interest: Shows Japan's 1930s codification of severance pay, prompted partly by American firms' liquidation questions.
overview: Docket (1930-36) on Japanese severance pay: a Chicago firm's 1934 inquiry on dismissing a 25-year employee, prompting Consul Chapman's report and ending with Japan's 1936 Law No. 42 on retirement allowances.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim at Tokyo

subfiles.about: A two-page State Department list of papers cataloguing correspondence, inquiries, and despatches from 1930 to 1936 concerning retirement allowances, dismissal pay, and employer-employee relations in Japan.
